title: 3. Qualifications and Disqualifications of Lok Sabha Members

blocks.content:
Qualifications:
• Citizen of India
• Minimum age – 25 years
• Should not hold office of profit
Disqualifications:
• Holding office of profit
• Unsound mind
• Insolvency
• Disqualification under anti-defection law
Should not hold office of profit

rows: Citizen of India; Minimum age – 25 years; Should not hold office of profit
Holding office of profit; Unsound mind; Insolvency; Disqualification under anti-defection law

items: Remember the minimum age for Lok Sabha is 25 years, whereas for Rajya Sabha it is 30 years.
Disqualification under the anti-defection law is a crucial topic frequently asked in Polity prelims and mains.
'Office of profit' serves as both a qualification restriction and a ground for disqualification.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: An individual must be a citizen of India and at least 25 years of age to qualify for Lok Sabha membership.
Candidates are prohibited from holding an office of profit.
Disqualification can be triggered by holding an office of profit, unsound mind, or insolvency.
Members are subject to disqualification under the anti-defection law.
